info.description: Creates the same resources as thunderid-config/thunderid-config.yaml through the ThunderID management API, then onboards a company and plugs its identity provider into the shared sign-in flow. Run the folders in order.

request.description: Signs in as a ThunderID administrator through the Console client and stores a token with the system permission.

item.name: 01 - Create the Wayfinder Enterprise organization unit

request.description: A root organization unit. Every company that signs up becomes a child of it.
Owned by the parent unit, so every company beneath it can use it.

item.name: 03 - Create the Wayfinder Enterprise API resource server

body.raw:
{
  "name": "Wayfinder Admin",
  "description": "Manages a company's travel policy, team and enterprise sign-in",
  "ouId": "{{parentOuId}}",
  "permissions": [
    {
      "resourceServerId": "{{apiResourceServerId}}",
      "permissions": [
        "booking:view",
        "booking:create",
        "booking:manage",
        "policy:view",
        "policy:manage",
        "user:view",
        "user:manage",
        "group:view",
        "group:manage",
        "role:view",
        "role:manage",
        "sso:view",
        "sso:manage"
      ]
    }
  ]
}

item.name: 24 - Share the Wayfinder Admin role with every company
26 - Share the Wayfinder Member role with every company

request.description: Creates the company as a child of the parent unit, creates its first user inside it, and assigns the Wayfinder Admin role.
A password, or enterprise SSO through the identity provider the company selects for the enterpriseIdp variable.

item.name: 29 - Share the sign-in flow and let each company set enterpriseIdp

request.description: Wayfinder's blue and yellow, and Inter, for the sign-in and sign-up screens.
A centered card on Wayfinder's background. With a theme or a layout assigned, the screens drop ThunderID's own branding.

item.name: 33 - Share the application with every company

request.description: The confidential client the app backend uses for the root-only management calls it makes on a company admin's behalf. It is owned by the Wayfinder Enterprise organization unit and names the company in its tokens.

item.name: 35 - Share the backend application with every company

request.description: Lets the backend request a token for any company at /ou/{ouId}/oauth2/token.

item.name: 36 - Create the backend role and assign it to the backend application

request.description: Grants the root system permission to the backend application. The role is assigned in the application's own organization unit, because only those roles count when it gets a token for a company.
The same flow ThunderID's sign-up page runs when someone chooses Register your company in the app.
The first step of the sign-up flow. A taken username returns this step again.
Completes with flowStatus COMPLETE. The company is created under the parent unit with its admin inside it. A taken organization handle returns this step again.

item.name: 05 - Get a backend token for the company

request.description: The backend application's client credentials at the company's token endpoint. The token names the company in its ouId, and the requests after it use it, as the app's admin routes do.

item.name: 06 - Create the company's OpenID Connect identity provider

request.description: Owned by the company. Register {{baseUrl}}/gate/callback as the callback URL at the identity provider. In the app, the OIDCConnectionCreate component does this.

item.name: 07 - Plug the identity provider into the sign-in flow for the company

request.description: Sets the company's value of the shared sign-in flow's enterpriseIdp variable. In the app, the FlowConnectionBinding component does this.
